title: polyglot-cursor-checkpointing-for-embeddings-to-rerank-alpha
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Goal: Implement a resumable, language-consistent cursor+checkpoint model for the embeddings -> rerank SDK workflow (Python, TypeScript, Go). This ticket designs and prototypes a StreamCheckpointIterator shim that: 1) yields items as (cursorToken, id, vector) for safe replay and idempotent rerank requests; 2) persists lightweight checkpoints to user-provided storage or an SDK-managed ephemeral store; 3) exposes backpressure-friendly streaming APIs that map cleanly to Python async generators, TS async iterators, and Go channels; and 4) provides hooks for per-batch telemetry (tokens, vector bytes, latency) to surface cost/latency at route/model granularity.

Background: Existing SDK helpers focus on pagination and batching for embeddings and rerank, but implementations diverge across languages in retry semantics and streaming ergonomics. Users building large rerank pipelines need the ability to pause/replay a stream (for transient infra errors or to resume after canary switches), measure per-batch economics, and ensure exact-once semantics when forwarding vectors to the reranker.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Design cross-language API contracts and polyfills for streaming checkpoints that do not require users to implement complex control-flow.
- Prototype in Python, TypeScript, and Go with parity in behavior for: pause/resume, checkpoint format, retry idempotency token, and telemetry hooks.
- Provide clear examples showing: small-batch synchronous mode, large-window streaming mode with resume after failure, and a streaming-to-rerank composition helper that transforms embedding stream to batched rerank requests.
- Add unit and integration tests covering resume after network errors, duplicate suppression, and checkpoint corruption heuristics.
- Document trade-offs and migration guidance in the SDK CHANGELOG and Confluence.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Checkpoint format: use compact base64-encoded cursor + epoch + sequence number to keep token small and language-agnostic. Advantage: tiny storage footprint and easy to pass in URLs. Trade-off: requires base64 helpers in some constrained runtimes.
- Storage surface: SDK accepts either a user-supplied checkpoint store (callable/object) or the SDK-managed ephemeral filesystem/Redis adapter. We default to user store in production to avoid hidden state; SDK provides a Redis adapter for quick tests.
- Exactly-once vs at-least-once: we implement idempotency keys and duplicate suppression in the rerank helper but document that full exactly-once requires server-side support. This keeps SDK lightweight.
- Backpressure: provide a tunable buffer_size parameter and conservative defaults (buffer_size=3). This avoids unbounded memory growth but can increase end-to-end latency for synchronous workloads.

Polyglot API sketches (for reviewers):
- Python (recommended):
  - class StreamCheckpointIterator:
    - __init__(source, checkpoint_store=None, buffer_size=3)
    - async __aiter__() -> yields {"cursor": str, "id": str, "vector": List[float]}
    - async checkpoint(cursor_token: str)
    - async resume(cursor_token: str)

- TypeScript (recommended):
  - interface CheckpointItem { cursor: string; id: string; vector: number[] }
  - function streamWithCheckpoints(source: AsyncIterable<CheckpointItem>, opts): AsyncIterable<CheckpointItem>
  - opts.checkpointStore: { save(token), load() }

- Go (recommended):
  - type CheckpointItem struct { Cursor string; ID string; Vector []float64 }
  - func StreamWithCheckpoints(ctx context.Context, src <-chan CheckpointItem, opts Options) (<-chan CheckpointItem, error)

Migration guide highlights:
- Existing users of pagination helpers can opt into StreamCheckpointIterator via a single wrapper call; no changes to server endpoints required.
- Example code snippets and a notebook (Drive link below) show typical conversions from sync list->batch rerank to streaming-resume flows.

Artifact links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/882104/Stream+Checkpoint+Iterator+Design
- Prototype PR (monorepo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1246
- Integration test job: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/jobs/stream-checkpoint-e2e/12
- Design notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3C_stream_checkpoint_examples

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: language runtime differences lead to subtle behavior gaps. Mitigation: canonical behavior tests (Python<->TS<->Go) that run the same vectors and assert identical checkpoint tokens and replay behavior.
- Risk: users rely on SDK-managed ephemeral store and lose state. Mitigation: clear docs and warnings; default to no SDK-managed persistence in production builds.

Open questions:
- Should SDK encrypt checkpoint tokens by default (adds complexity but improves security)? (PO/Prod opinion: flag behind release toggle.)
- Do we want a first-class server-side API for checkpoint verification to enable stronger exactly-once guarantees? (Follow-up epics if demand high.)
